applicable_when: The kernel performs a layout permutation from contiguous NCHW (stride=(150528,50176,224,1)) to channels-last-like output (stride=(150528,1,672,3)). The load `in_ptr0 + (x2 + 50176*y3)` is stride-1 contiguous in x2 (XBLOCK dimension) and can be vectorized to 128-bit. The store `out_ptr0 + (y0 + 3*x2 + 150528*y1)` writes with stride-3 in x2 (consecutive threads write addresses 3 apart), causing 23% excessive sectors and only 20/32 bytes utilized per sector. Adding tl.max_contiguous and tl.multiple_of hints on the load offset tells the compiler the access is XBLOCK-aligned and contiguous, enabling 128-bit (float4) vectorized loads. Increasing XBLOCK from 128 to 512 and decreasing YBLOCK from 8 to 2 processes more contiguous x-elements per CTA, improving L1 cache reuse on the load side and amortizing launch overhead.
